Lancaster County by the numbers

What is Lancaster County, Nebraska, and where do its towns sit?

Lancaster County covers about 846 square miles, with Lincoln as the county seat and the state capital. Of that area, roughly 838 square miles are land.

Four cities lie inside it: Bennet, Hickman, Lincoln and Waverly. The villages are Davey, Denton, Firth, Hallam, Malcolm, Panama, Raymond, Roca and Sprague. Census-designated places include Agnew, Cheney, Emerald, Kramer, Martell, Prairie Home, Princeton, Walton and Yankee Hill, and Arbor, Berks, Holland, Rokeby and Saltillo are other unincorporated communities. Neighbors are Saunders, Cass, Otoe, Johnson, Gage, Saline, Seward and Butler counties.

Because the county holds both a capital city and small villages, a sale can involve a house in Lincoln, an acreage near Branched Oak Lake or a village home in Hallam, and the same county offices process each of them.

How did Lancaster County form?

Lancaster County was created on March 16, 1855 and organized on October 10, 1859. Gage County, its southern neighbor, was created on the very same day.

It is also one of the most urban counties in Nebraska. The 2020 census put 90.3 percent of residents in urban areas, and the median age was 34.7 years. Bryan Health, a Lincoln-based health system, says it has over 7,000 employees and calls itself one of the largest employers in Nebraska. A county this urban handles far more transactions on city lots than on farm ground, and the treasurer's office collects tax for schools, fire districts, cities and villages alike.

What do the 2020 census figures show for Lancaster County?

Lancaster County had 322,608 residents in the 2020 census, with 127,884 households and 135,484 housing units. The table gathers the sourced numbers.

A homeowner vacancy rate of 1.0 percent means few owner-occupied homes sat empty in 2020. Landlords hold a large share of the stock, since more than four in ten occupied homes were rented, so a house with a tenant in place is a realistic situation for sellers here.

How do people get around Lancaster County?

Interstate 80 and Interstate 180 serve the county, along with US Highways 6, 34 and 77 and Nebraska Highways 2, 33, 43 and 79. Amtrak's California Zephyr stops at the Lincoln station, and Burlington Trailways, Express Arrow and the city's StarTran bus service round out public transport.

The county also has a long list of recreation areas, including Branched Oak, Pawnee, Conestoga, Stagecoach, Wagon Train, Olive Creek and Bluestem lakes, plus Holmes Lake and Pioneers Park Nature Center.

The National Weather Service named Lancaster County a StormReady county in 2004. Weather risk is relevant to roofs and insurance, so keep roof age and any prior claims handy for buyers and inspectors.

When are Lancaster County property taxes due and delinquent?

Lancaster County taxes are due December 31 each year, and because the county has more than 100,000 residents, Nebraska statute 77-204 makes the first half delinquent April 1 and the second half August 1. Smaller counties use May 1 and September 1, so the calendar differs from most of the state.

  • The treasurer's walk-in office is at 555 S. 10th Street, Room 102, Lincoln, open Monday through Friday from 7:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
  • Questions about the online property search can go to (402) 441-7425 or cotreasurer@lancaster.ne.gov.
  • You can pay real estate and personal property taxes electronically through your bank or a bill payment service.
  • The county treasurer's property search shows each parcel's rate and tax district.

As an example of how the rate shows up, one Lincoln parcel in tax district 0001 on the treasurer's site lists a 2025 tax rate of 1.6662840 percent, and a parcel in a tax increment financing district south of downtown shows the same figure. Rates differ by district, so check the parcel you are selling instead of assuming a countywide rate.

How do you protest a Lancaster County valuation?

Lancaster County protests are filed with the County Clerk from June 1 through June 30 each year on Form 422. The county's protest notice states that forms received before June 1 or postmarked after June 30 cannot be accepted as timely filed.

The form must give the property description and the reason for the request, and the County Board of Equalization hears the protests. Nebraska's state rules route an unhappy outcome to the Tax Equalization and Review Commission within 30 days after the county board adjourns. The Lancaster County Assessor/Register of Deeds is a combined, elected office with general supervision of the assessment of all property in the county, and its number is (402) 441-8776.

The county board's minutes for August 4, 2026 include a Form 422 dismissals item, which shows that decisions on protests can continue well after the June filing window closes. Because the filing window itself is only 30 days, collect photographs, repair quotes and nearby sales before June 1.

What should a Lancaster County seller check about taxes before closing?

The earlier April 1 and August 1 delinquency dates make timing the main thing to check, because a first-half payment that would still be on time elsewhere in Nebraska is already late in Lancaster County. Three checks help:

  • Look up the parcel on the treasurer's property information search to see whether both halves of the prior year are paid.
  • Ask the closing agent whether the current-year bill will be paid in full from your proceeds or split with the buyer.
  • Confirm the mailing address on file, since statements follow the address given on the transfer statement filed with the deed.

The treasurer's site states that it furnishes parcel information as a public service and makes no warranty about it, so treat the online figure as a starting point and confirm a payoff in writing before closing.

How are deeds recorded in Lancaster County?

Deeds are recorded at the Register of Deeds, 555 South 10th Street in Lincoln, for $10.00 on the first page and $6.00 for each added page. A deed must come with a completed Real Estate Transfer Statement, Form 521, and the documentary stamp tax where it applies.

The office recommends emailing a copy to RegDeed@lancaster.ne.gov before mailing the original so staff can check recordability and fees. You can also record electronically through contracted vendors, and the county adds no charge for e-filing, though each vendor sets its own fee. The office phone is 402-441-7463, and it cannot complete documents or give legal advice.

The Register of Deeds is a recording office only, and its forms page includes the Certificate of Exemption for the documentary stamp tax (form 5b). The state rate is $3.32 per $1,000 of value for deeds recorded on or after July 18, 2026, and the seller pays it as grantor.

When are Lancaster County property taxes delinquent?

The first half becomes delinquent April 1 and the second half August 1. Counties with more than 100,000 people follow that schedule under Nebraska statute 77-204, while smaller counties use May 1 and September 1.

What is the Lancaster County protest period?

Protests on Form 422 are accepted with the County Clerk from June 1 through June 30. Forms received before June 1 or postmarked after June 30 are not timely.

Where is the Lancaster County treasurer's office?

The walk-in office is at 555 S. 10th Street, Room 102, Lincoln, and it keeps Monday through Friday hours of 7:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. You can also pay electronically through a bank bill payment service.

How much does it cost to record a deed in Lancaster County?

The filing fee is $10.00 for the first page and $6.00 for each additional page. You also need Form 521 and any documentary stamp tax, which is $3.32 per $1,000 of value after July 18, 2026.

Is the Lancaster County tax rate the same across the county?

No. Rates depend on the tax district, and the treasurer's property search shows the rate for each parcel. One Lincoln district listing showed 1.6662840 percent for tax year 2025.

Where is Gage County, Nebraska, and what is in it?

Gage County lies on Nebraska's southern edge, with its southern boundary touching Kansas, and Beatrice is the county seat. The county covers about 860 square miles, of which about 851 are land, and the Big Blue River runs south-southeast through its middle.

It has three cities, Beatrice, Blue Springs and Wymore, and nine villages: Adams, Barneston, Clatonia, Cortland, Filley, Liberty, Odell, Pickrell and Virginia. Holmesville is a census-designated place, and Ellis, Hoag, Krider, Lanham and Rockford are unincorporated communities. Lancaster County, home to Lincoln, is the northern neighbor.

The National Park Service puts Beatrice about 40 miles south of Lincoln and about 100 miles south of Omaha. Gage County's northern edge meets Lancaster County, so Lincoln is the nearest large city for much of the county.

How did Gage County begin?

Gage County was created on March 16, 1855 and organized in 1857, from land taken from the Otoe in an 1854 treaty. It was named for William D. Gage, a Methodist minister who served as the first chaplain of the Nebraska Territorial Legislature.

The county's best-known landmark is tied to that settlement era. Homestead National Historical Park, authorized on March 19, 1936 and covering about 211 acres, sits roughly five miles northwest of Beatrice and commemorates the Homestead Act. Parcels in a county settled this early are described by legal description, and a title company will want to read that description and the recorded history before closing.

What do the Census numbers show for Gage County housing?

Gage County counted 21,704 residents in the 2020 census, and the 2025 estimate is 21,711, so the population has held roughly steady. The table lists the sourced figures.

ItemFigureSource year
Population21,7042020 census
Households9,2842020 census
Housing units10,327, with 10.1% vacant2020 census
Owner-occupied share70.3%2020 census
Renter-occupied share29.7%2020 census
Median age44.2 years2020 census
Urban share of residents55.9%2020 census

Nearly three in ten occupied homes were rented in 2020, so landlords form a real part of the seller pool. Highways US 77, US 136 and Nebraska 4, 8, 41, 43, 103 and 112 connect the towns.

How does the Gage County assessor value a home?

The assessor values most homes by replacement cost new less depreciation, plus land, then tests the results against sales within defined market areas. For residential and commercial property the target is 92 to 100 percent of market value, and for agricultural land it is 69 to 75 percent.

Residential values rely on a two-year sales study, while agricultural and commercial values use three years, and the study period ends June 30 of the preceding year. State law has the office review each property at least every six years. Field staff drive county vehicles and wear name badges and bright green vests.

  • A market neighborhood can include as many as 500 homes, so the assessor values by group, not by single sale.
  • Commercial property is often valued by an income approach, and income information sent to the office stays confidential.
  • Your mailing address for tax statements comes from line 19 of the Form 521 transfer statement filed with your deed.
  • Greenbelt status for qualifying farmland requires Form 456 before August 1.

How do you protest a Gage County valuation?

You protest the valuation, never the tax itself, by filing Form 422 in triplicate with the County Board of Equalization at the county clerk's office, 612 Grant Street in Beatrice. Real property protests are due on or before June 30, personal property protests by May 1, and a protest that does not state the requested value and the reasons can be dismissed.

The assessor's office suggests you first ask an appraiser to explain how your value was reached, which gives the office a chance to fix errors. After a hearing, the board notifies you of its decision within seven days. A further appeal goes to the Tax Equalization and Review Commission within 30 days after the board adjourns, with July 25 deemed the adjournment date for the June 1 to July 25 session.

Useful evidence is a showing that the assessor valued your property above market value or out of line with similar properties.

When are Gage County taxes due, and what are the payment options?

Real estate and personal property taxes in Gage County are due December 31, the first half becomes delinquent the following May 1 and the second half on September 1, and a 14 percent statutory rate applies to delinquencies. Notices are mailed in December.

  • Online payments run through nto.us, with a 2.49 percent convenience fee for a card and $1.75 for an e-check.
  • Card payments are also taken at the treasurer's office, at the same fee.
  • The treasurer's office phone is (402) 223-1319, as printed in the county's 2026 tax sale notice.
  • If your address is wrong, call or use the county's change of address form.

Gage County adds a few rules for mobile homes. The county does not prorate taxes on a sold mobile home, so buyer and seller must split them. A moving permit is not issued until taxes are paid up to date, and moving without that step is a class four misdemeanor. If the new owner never files forms 521 and 402, the tax statement stays in the seller's name.

How does the Gage County tax sale work?

The Gage County treasurer holds an annual public tax sale in March, and the 2026 sale was set for March 2 at 9:00 a.m. in the district courtroom on the third floor of the courthouse. Delinquent parcels are advertised for three consecutive weeks in February in the Beatrice Daily Sun.

Bidders register in advance, pay a $25 registration fee, and take turns choosing parcels round-robin under Nebraska statute 77-1807. A buyer gets a tax lien, not the property, and a certificate not redeemed within three years opens the way to foreclosure, with strict notice deadlines before three years and nine months. Redemption pays the buyer 14 percent interest. Purchasers add an automatic $150 administrative fee for serving notice on the owner, which the owner pays at redemption.

The county does not sell tax certificates on properties in bankruptcy or on parcels owned by government entities. Owners who want to avoid the notice step and extra fees usually clear the balance or sell before the February advertising run.

What should Gage County sellers know about exemptions and recording?

Homestead exemption applicants, generally owners over 65 and certain disabled people and veterans, must file between February 1 and June 30 every year in the assessor's office. You lose the exemption if you sell or leave the home before August 15, though if you buy another Nebraska home before that date you can file a transfer statement to move it.

At closing, Nebraska's documentary stamp tax is $3.32 per $1,000 of value for deeds recorded on or after July 18, 2026, paid by the seller as grantor. Zoning and building permits, including setbacks, are checked by legal description and address with county planning, and a permit application needs two identical sets of plans.

More questions about Gage County, NE Property Tax Guide

When are Gage County property taxes due?

They are due December 31. The first half is delinquent the following May 1 and the second half the following September 1, with a 14 percent statutory rate on delinquencies.

Can I protest my Gage County property tax bill?

You cannot protest the bill, only the valuation. File Form 422 with the county clerk in Beatrice by June 30 for real property, stating the value you want and why.

What fees apply when paying Gage County taxes by card?

The county FAQ lists a 2.49 percent convenience fee for credit or debit cards and $1.75 for an e-check. Real estate taxes can be paid online at nto.us.

Does Gage County prorate taxes when a mobile home is sold?

No. The county does not prorate taxes on mobile homes, so buyer and seller split them. The new owner must also file forms 521 and 402 with the assessor or the bill stays in the seller's name.

Can I sell a Gage County house that is in the tax sale list?

Yes, provided the delinquent taxes and charges are paid at closing. If a certificate has already been sold, the owner also owes the buyer's interest and a $150 service fee to redeem.

Where is Saunders County and how is it laid out?

Saunders County is an eastern Nebraska county of about 760 square miles, and its county seat and largest city is Wahoo. The county is counted as part of the Omaha-Council Bluffs metropolitan area, yet most of its land is farm ground.

The county's own description says the Platte River borders it on the north and east and that the terrain is low rolling hills sloping toward the river valley. About 750 square miles are land and roughly 10 square miles are water.

Population at the 2020 census was 22,278. The Nebraska Association of County Officials fact sheet splits that between three cities, eleven villages and the countryside:

  • Wahoo: 4,818 residents
  • Ashland: 3,086 residents
  • Yutan: 1,347 residents
  • Villages including Ceresco, Mead, Cedar Bluffs, Valparaiso, Memphis, Prague and Weston
  • Unincorporated areas: 9,045 residents, about 41 percent of the county

That 41 percent matters for anyone selling. A large share of Saunders County homes sit on acreage outside a city limit, where the rules about wells, zoning and roads differ from a lot in Wahoo.

How did Saunders County get its name and its county seat?

Saunders County was created by the territorial legislature on January 26, 1856 under the name Calhoun County, and it was renamed in 1862 for Alvin Saunders, the territorial governor. Settlers disliked the first name because a government surveyor called Calhoun was suspected of corruption.

Ashland, believed to be the first settlement, served as the first county seat and built a courthouse in 1870. Voters chose the more central town of Wahoo in 1873. The courthouse standing at 433 N Chestnut today was built in 1904 for $87,000, and the Register of Deeds, Assessor and Treasurer still work from it.

A torpedo replica on the courthouse lawn memorializes the U.S.S. Wahoo and its crew of 65. The county page also notes that Wahoo once had John F. Kennedy College, which won the first three softball tournaments later known as the Women's College World Series.

What does the Saunders County economy run on?

Farming and the businesses that serve it carry most of the Saunders County economy, with manufacturing and services behind them. The county fact sheet reports that 89 percent of the land is in agriculture, with corn on 40 percent and soybeans on 36 percent.

MeasureFigureYear
County gross domestic product$1,100,460,0002023
Farm and ranch commodity sales$514,932,0002022
Nonfarm wage income of residents$688,280,0002022
Unemployment rate2.2%March 2025
Ethanol capacity (Chief Ethanol Fuels)55 million gallons a yearfact sheet
Housing units9,9872020
Owner-occupied rate79.6%2020

One footnote is worth knowing. The wage figure follows where a worker lives, so it includes pay earned in other counties by Saunders County residents. Some residents earn their pay in other counties, so the income figure and the local job base are not the same thing.

Rail serves Leshara, Mead, Valparaiso, Wahoo, Weston and Yutan, and the county lists grain elevators in Ceresco, Colon, Mead, Prague, Wahoo and Weston.

Which offices handle property tax in Saunders County?

Three offices in the courthouse at 433 N Chestnut, Wahoo, NE 68066 split the work: the Assessor values, the Treasurer bills and collects, and the Register of Deeds records the transfer.

  • Assessor (Suite 200, 402-443-5600): values every parcel in the county. Rhonda Andresen holds the office, with Sara Stuchlik as deputy.
  • Treasurer (Suite 201, 402-443-8128, mail to PO Box 337): bills and collects real estate and personal property tax and sends the money to schools, cities and other districts. The same office also handles motor vehicle registration and driver licensing.
  • Register of Deeds (Suite 203, 402-443-8111): records deeds and mortgages. Deeds from 1997 forward can be searched on Nebraska Deeds Online.

Offices open 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Monday through Friday. The Treasurer notes that a new title needs to be in the door by 4:00 p.m. Payments can also be made through the state's Nebraska Taxes Online page for Saunders County.

How does the assessor value a Saunders County property?

The Saunders County Assessor values property as of 12:01 a.m. on January 1 each tax year, at 100 percent of market value for homes, commercial and industrial property and at 75 percent for agricultural and horticultural land. That is the county's own summary of state law.

The assessor's job is to set the value. The tax rate comes from the county board and every other taxing body, and it is applied to that value. A seller who disagrees with a value works through the protest window the county board handles, not through the Treasurer.

Nebraska also requires the person running an assessment office to hold a certification from the Department of Property Assessment and Taxation and to keep up continuing education hours. The state's section 77-201 sets the 75 percent rule for farmland, with a lower 50 percent figure for school bond levies approved by voters on or after January 1, 2022.

What do Saunders County levy numbers look like?

The county's own levy was $0.2160 per $100 of taxable valuation in the fact sheet's 2024 data, and it raised about $12.0 million of a local-government total near $75.6 million. The county board's slice is therefore roughly 16 percent of what property owners in the county pay in total to all local bodies.

2024 itemAmount
County levy rate$0.2160 per $100
County property taxes levied$12,026,691
All local government property taxes levied$75,635,941
Countywide taxable valuation$5,567,290,017

As a plain illustration, a house valued at $250,000 would carry about $540 of county levy ($250,000 divided by 100, times 0.2160). Schools, the city or village, the natural resource district and other bodies add their own levies on top, so the county line is never the whole bill. The Department of Revenue posts every rate in its annual taxing subdivisions report.

Why can two similar houses in Saunders County pay different tax?

Two similar houses can pay different tax because Saunders County is cut into many school districts and village limits, and each combination has its own total levy. The county fact sheet lists 13 school districts serving parts of the county, among them Ashland-Greenwood, Wahoo, Yutan, Mead, Cedar Bluffs, Raymond Central and North Bend Central, plus districts named for Fremont, Gretna, Schuyler, Waverly and David City.

Lower Platte North and Lower Platte South are the two natural resource districts that reach into the county. A buyer comparing a Wahoo address with an Ashland address, or a town lot with an acreage, should ask for the actual prior-year bill, not a county average.

Electric service also varies by location. The fact sheet names Butler PPD, the City of Wahoo, Omaha PPD and the Village of Prague as providers, which is a useful line in a listing or a cash-offer conversation about monthly carrying costs.

What changes at closing when you sell a Saunders County house?

At closing the seller pays Nebraska's documentary stamp tax, and the title company settles the current year's property tax between the two sides. Under section 76-901, the tax falls on the grantor at $3.32 for each $1,000 of value for transfers before January 1, 2032, then drops to $2.32.

On a $250,000 sale that works out to $830. Value means the full consideration, including any liens the buyer assumes, and a fraction of $1,000 counts as a full $1,000.

Deeds between spouses, between ex-spouses dividing marital property, or between parent and child with no actual payment are exempt under section 76-902(5)(a). Families passing a house down inside Saunders County should confirm the exemption wording with the Register of Deeds before recording.

  • Ask the title company for a written tax proration before you sign.
  • Check that every delinquent installment is included in the payoff figures.
  • Record the deed in Wahoo, then confirm the Assessor has the new owner's mailing address.

The Register of Deeds also offers a free Property Fraud Alert that emails an owner when a document is recorded under their name, which is worth setting up for any house that will sit vacant before a sale.

What should rural and acreage sellers in Saunders County check first?

Rural sellers should check water, zoning and land classification first, because a Saunders County farmstead is valued and regulated differently from a town lot. The county fact sheet counts 1,500 rural drinking water wells and says state law does not require registration of small wells drilled before September 9, 1993, so a missing record is not unusual for an older place.

  • Wells that can pump more than 50 gallons a minute must be registered and permitted through the local natural resource district.
  • The fact sheet lists Saunders County as a zoned county, so ask the county before assuming a land split or second dwelling is allowed.
  • Dryland crop ground covers 51 percent of the county's land and irrigated ground 23 percent, and the mix on a parcel affects its farm valuation.

Nebraska's seller disclosure law, section 76-2,120, asks sellers of one-to-four-unit residential property to state the condition of the electrical, heating, water and sewer systems in writing. A fiduciary selling for an estate is generally excused unless that person lived in the home.

More questions about Saunders County, NE Property Tax Guide

Where do I pay Saunders County property tax?

Pay the Saunders County Treasurer at 433 N Chestnut, Suite 201, in Wahoo, mail to PO Box 337, or use the Nebraska Taxes Online page the county links from its Treasurer page. The office phone is 402-443-8128.

How do I find a recorded deed in Saunders County?

Deeds from 1997 to the present are searchable on Nebraska Deeds Online for Saunders County. For older records, call the Register of Deeds at 402-443-8111, Suite 203 of the Wahoo courthouse.

Do I owe stamp tax if I deed my house to my child?

Not if no actual payment changes hands. Nebraska exempts deeds between parent and child without actual consideration under section 76-902(5)(a). A sale at a stated price is taxed at $3.32 per $1,000 before 2032.

Is farmland assessed the same as a house in Saunders County?

No. The Assessor values homes and commercial property at 100 percent of market value and agricultural and horticultural land at 75 percent, as of January 1.

Who pays the current year's tax when a Saunders County house sells mid-year?

The purchase contract and the title company decide how the year is split. Ask for the proration in writing, and make sure any delinquent installment is paid from your proceeds at closing.

Where is Cass County, Nebraska, and how did it start?

Cass County is bounded on the north by the Platte River and on the east by the Missouri River, with Plattsmouth as the county seat. The county's About page says the territorial legislature approved it on March 7, 1855, and named it for General Lewis Cass of Michigan. It measures roughly 34 miles east to west and 20 miles north to south.

Wikipedia gives a 2020 census population of 26,598 and a 2025 estimate of 27,657. Plattsmouth is the largest city. The town began in 1852 as a ferry point on the Missouri River, and its name comes from its position at the meeting of the Platte and Missouri.

The county describes itself as one of the earliest settled in Nebraska. Many early towns have since vanished, and fifteen remain.

  • Cards are not accepted for tax sale redemptions.

The Assessor's page says the office handles about 21,000 real estate parcels and 1,300 personal property parcels, processes over 900 homestead applications and 150 permissive exemption applications, and answers about 10,000 information requests a year.

  • Rural townships: Mount Pleasant, Center, Weeping Water, Avoca/Nehawka and Nehawka/Liberty

Collectors wear orange reflective vests, carry county badges issued by the Sheriff's Office and drive county vehicles. They photograph and measure structures. If nobody is home, they leave a call-back slip on the door. Owners can return a property review questionnaire by mail or in the drop box on the west side of the courthouse.

If you own a house in one of those areas and plan to sell, a reappraisal visit is a good time to confirm that the square footage, finished basement and outbuildings on record match what is actually there. Errors in that record affect the value your future buyer will be taxed on.

How do I protest a property value in Cass County?

Use Form 422. The Assessor's page links Form 422 with instructions, and the county has a separate Property Valuation Protest page. The Assessor's page also links to the state's Tax Equalization and Review Commission for later steps.

Other deadlines on the Assessor's page:

  • Homestead exemption applications are due between February 2 and June 30.
  • Personal property filings are due on or before May 1.
  • The Assessor reviews applications for religious, charitable and educational exemptions.

The Assessor is an elected official with a four-year term and must hold a state certificate and complete 15 hours of continuing education each year.

How does the Cass County tax sale work?

The county's 2025 information sheet says the sale ran at the Plattsmouth Community Center, 308 S. 18th St., starting at 8 a.m., and that delinquent taxes are advertised for three weeks in February in the Sarpy County Times.

  • Buyers pay a $25 registration fee and $20 per certificate.
  • The sale uses a round robin format, where a random first bidder gets the first parcel.
  • Buyers acquire a lien, not the property, and they cannot foreclose for three years.
  • The Treasurer does not issue treasurer's deeds, so foreclosure goes through the courts.
  • Parcels already on a tax sale, in bankruptcy, or owned by government are not sold.

The notice states that published amounts do not include delinquent interest and may cover several years. If your house is on the list, get a current payoff in writing, because a sale to a buyer lets the title company clear the amount at closing.

What happens at closing when a Cass County house sells?

The Nebraska documentary stamp tax applies to the deed. The Department of Revenue lists the rate at $3.32 per $1,000 of value for deeds recorded on or after July 18, 2026 (older regulation text still shows $2.25). The regulations make the grantor liable and allow the grantee or any agent presenting the deed to pay it. Deeds are recorded through the Cass County Register of Deeds, which has an online deed search.

The Assessor's office also keeps a sales file for every property sale in the county and checks it against its records, according to its services list. That file is one reason an unusually low sale price may draw a data collector's visit later, which is worth knowing if you are pricing a quick as-is sale.

Form 422, which the Assessor's page links with instructions. The county also has a Property Valuation Protest page.

The Treasurer's notice says no. A certificate holder must foreclose through the courts, and there are statutory time limits on certificates.

Where is Fillmore County, Nebraska, and how is it laid out?

Fillmore County sits in southeastern Nebraska, with Geneva as the county seat and a total area of about 577 square miles, of which roughly 575 are land. Its neighbors are York, Seward, Saline, Jefferson, Thayer, Nuckolls, Clay and Hamilton counties.

The land is part of the eastern loess plain, a wind-laid silt surface that slopes toward the southeast. Water drains to the Big Blue River system through the West Fork of the Big Blue, Turkey Creek and the Little Blue. In places the flat uplands hold shallow, short-lived wetlands after heavy rain or snowmelt, which is worth knowing if a property you are selling sits on low ground.

The county's only city is Geneva. The villages are Exeter, Fairmont, Grafton, Milligan, Ohiowa, Shickley and Strang, and the 2020 census counted every resident as rural.

How did Fillmore County get its start?

The Nebraska Territorial Legislature defined the county in 1856, and the county's own website lists January 26, 1856 as the establishment date and May 27, 1871 as the date it was organized. It was named for Millard Fillmore, the thirteenth president.

The railroad shaped where people settled. The Burlington and Missouri River line came through in 1871 and its towns along the route, Exeter, Fairmont and Grafton, were named in alphabetical order, a habit of that railroad. Before the county was organized it had been administered and taxed from neighboring Saline County. The county seat site was first platted as Henry and renamed Geneva in 1872.

Settlement of the 1870s means some Fillmore County houses and farmsteads are very old. If you inherited one, the age of the roof, wiring and foundation is usually the first thing a buyer asks about.

What do the numbers say about Fillmore County homes and people?

Fillmore County had 5,551 residents in the 2020 census and an estimated 5,458 in 2025, so it is small and slowly shrinking. The table below keeps the sourced figures in one place.

A vacancy rate above 12 percent in the 2020 count means a house that needs work can sit a while on the open market. Sellers with a vacant inherited home or a rental they no longer want to manage often weigh that waiting time against the cost of holding the property through another tax cycle.

Which roads, rails and towns matter when you sell here?

US Route 81 enters from Thayer County and runs north into York County, US Route 6 crosses the northern part of the county, Nebraska Highway 41 runs through the middle and Highway 74 along the south. BNSF Railway tracks run east to west across the north, passing Exeter, Fairmont and Grafton.

A few practical points follow for a seller:

  • Houses along US 6 and the rail line in Exeter, Fairmont and Grafton draw a different pool than farmsteads off county gravel.
  • Geneva has the courthouse, the county offices and the schools, so it tends to anchor local interest.
  • Rural acreage may be taxed as agricultural land, which follows different valuation rules from a town lot.
  • Lots in low spots on the loess plain deserve a look at drainage before listing or inspection.

The Fillmore County Development Corporation, based at 1032 G Street in Geneva, works on local economic development and is a useful contact if you want a sense of local business activity.

When are Fillmore County property taxes due and delinquent?

Real estate and personal property taxes in Fillmore County become delinquent on May 1 and September 1 and interest starts on that date, citing Nebraska statutes 77-203 and 77-204. The delinquent interest rate is 14 percent, and tax notices are mailed around December 1.

If April 30 or August 31 lands on a weekend or holiday, the first business day after it is the last day to pay without interest. Mailed payments are judged by postmark. The treasurer no longer has to mail paid receipts, so enclose a self-addressed stamped envelope if you want one.

  • You can look up amounts and payment status on the Nebraska Taxes Online website, or call the treasurer.
  • A 2.35 percent convenience fee applies when you pay by credit or debit card.
  • If a notice never arrives, call the treasurer's office; not receiving one does not remove the due date.
  • Change a mailing address by calling or using the county's change of address form.

When a house changes hands in the first part of the year, the first half of the prior year's bill is often still open until May 1. Ask the closing agent to show exactly which half is being paid and by whom.

How do you challenge a Fillmore County valuation?

You challenge the valuation, not the tax bill, by filing Nebraska Form 422 with the county clerk, who staffs the County Board of Equalization, by June 30 for real property. The county's assessor section hosts the protest information, and the form itself comes from the Nebraska Department of Revenue.

State rules on the form require the protest to state the value you are requesting and why. Appeals of a board decision go to the Tax Equalization and Review Commission within 30 days after the board adjourns, and for the June 1 to July 25 session the adjournment date is deemed to be July 25.

Good evidence is usually a recent sale of a similar house nearby, a repair estimate that explains a lower condition, or proof that your property is valued out of line with comparable ones. If the house has a failing roof, a cracked foundation or other major defects, photos and contractor bids carry more weight than opinion.

What happens if Fillmore County taxes go unpaid?

Unpaid taxes can end up in the county treasurer's annual tax sale, held the first Monday in March at 9:00 a.m. at the courthouse. Delinquent parcels are advertised in the local paper for three consecutive weeks in February and on Nebraska Taxes Online.

The buyer is purchasing a tax lien, not the house. The redemption period is three years, the certificate earns 14 percent, and the buyer must pay later years' delinquent taxes to keep the certificate alive. If the owner has not redeemed by the end of three years, the certificate holder has six months to start foreclosure, according to the county's tax sale page.

For a seller this is a deadline worth respecting. Selling before the February advertising avoids a public listing of the parcel, and advertising charges are added to what a certificate buyer pays. The county treasurer cannot give legal advice, so a Nebraska attorney is the right person for questions about certificates and redemption.

What does the deed and transfer step cost in Nebraska?

Nebraska's documentary stamp tax is $3.32 for each $1,000 of value, or fraction of $1,000, on deeds recorded as of July 18, 2026, and it is imposed on the grantor, who is the seller. Every deed also needs a completed Real Estate Transfer Statement, Form 521, which the register of deeds will not accept if it is incomplete.

The state's own example sheet shows how the tax is computed, and exemptions exist for some transfers, such as certain deeds to trustees. A title company or closing attorney normally prepares both items. Ask for the figure on your estimated settlement statement so nothing surprises you at the table.

Taxes become delinquent on May 1 and September 1, with interest starting on those dates at 14 percent. If April 30 or August 31 falls on a weekend or holiday, you have the next business day to pay without interest.

Where do I file a property valuation protest in Fillmore County?

File Nebraska Form 422 with the county clerk, who handles the County Board of Equalization. Real property protests are due by June 30, and you must state the value you want and the reason.

Can I sell a Fillmore County house that has back taxes?

Yes. Delinquent taxes are normally paid from the sale proceeds at closing. Selling before the February advertising avoids a public listing, and the closing agent can request a payoff figure from the treasurer.

It is $3.32 for each $1,000 of value for deeds recorded on or after July 18, 2026, and the seller pays it. A $150,000 sale would work out to $498 under that rate, subject to any exemption that applies.

Who is the Fillmore County treasurer's office for tax questions?

The county treasurer collects real estate and personal property taxes and can be reached through the county website. Tax amounts and payment status are also shown on Nebraska Taxes Online.

Where is Richardson County, and why is it unusual?

Richardson County is the southeast corner of Nebraska, and the lowest point in the state is on the Missouri River where it leaves Nebraska for Kansas and Missouri. The county covers 555 square miles, of which 552 are land. Missouri is across the river to the east and Kansas lies to the south.

Branches and tributaries of the Big Nemaha River flow southeast across rolling hills and empty into the Missouri at the county's southeast corner. Numerous drainages cut the land, and most of it is farmed. Parts of the Ioway and Sac and Fox reservations sit in the southeast corner between Falls City, Rulo and Hiawatha, Kansas, and the village of Preston is inside the Sac and Fox reservation. If a parcel is near that area, ask the assessor and a title company how it is classified before you list it.

How did Richardson County get its start?

The county was created in 1854, the year the Kansas-Nebraska Act opened the territory to settlement, and was reorganized in 1855 by the first territorial legislature. It was named for William A. Richardson, an Illinois congressman who sponsored the act and became governor of Nebraska Territory in 1858.

The first courthouse went up in 1863. A second one, built in 1873, burned on May 7, 1919. Falls City, founded in 1857 beside a rock ledge on the Big Nemaha called the Falls of Nemaha, won out over Salem after a prolonged contest and was declared the permanent county seat in 1860. Railroads then drove its growth: the Atchison and Nebraska arrived in 1871, the Missouri Pacific in 1882, and Falls City became a division point in 1909. Its population peaked at 6,200 in 1950.

Which towns and schools make up Richardson County?

Besides Falls City and Humboldt, the county has eight villages: Barada, Dawson, Preston, Rulo, Salem, Shubert, Stella and Verdon. Nim City and Strausville are unincorporated communities.

How do roads and the weather shape a Richardson County house?

U.S. Highways 73 and 75 run north and south through the county, U.S. 159 runs east to the Rulo bridge into Missouri, and Nebraska Highway 8 runs west along the southern border. Falls City itself has a hot-summer humid continental climate. Its July mean daily high is 88.1 degrees Fahrenheit, and the record high is 114.

Severe weather is part of the local record. On May 30, 1879, an F4 tornado, the Irving, Kansas tornado, crossed Richardson County on a path 800 yards wide and 100 miles long, killing 18 people and injuring 60. A single storm from over a century ago does not tell you much about your roof, but a hail or wind claim on file does, and buyers will ask about it.

A protest goes on Form 422 to the County Clerk by June 30, one form per parcel, with your reasons, the value you want and documents the board can use to reach it. A parcel that did not sell is still delinquent. If yours appears on the unsold list, the tax is still owed and still needs a plan.

The title company gets the tax payoff from the treasurer, and the seller pays the documentary stamp tax collected by the register of deeds. The state rate is $3.32 per $1,000 of value for deeds recorded on or after July 18, 2026. Form 521 goes with the deed.

Omaha's economy grew beyond farming and meatpacking into insurance, telecommunications and finance, and Wikipedia ties part of that shift to the Trans-Mississippi Exposition.

What we can say from the Assessor's FAQ is how value gets set. The Assessor/Register of Deeds' office tracks sale prices, because every sale is recorded in the same office, and compares each one with the last assessed value. When prices in an area rise or fall significantly, a revaluation follows. A house selling for a different price than its assessment is therefore a signal the office reads.

Who handles property tax in Douglas County, and how do I reach them?

The Assessor/Register of Deeds sets value, the Board of Equalization hears protests, and the Treasurer collects. Each has its own contact line:

  • Treasurer: (402) 444-7103, Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.; mail to PO Box 2855, Omaha, NE 68103.
  • Assessor, value questions: (402) 444-7060 or valuationissues@douglascounty-ne.gov.
  • Board of Equalization: (402) 444-6510 or Protest@douglascounty-ne.gov.

The Treasurer's real property page lists ways to pay: in person (cash, check, money order, or card with fees), a drop box for checks and money orders, by phone with a card, online by card, PayPal or e-check at $1.50, and by mail. The Assessor, not the Treasurer, controls the mailing address on file, so change it through the Assessor's form to keep your statement coming.

When is Douglas County property tax due?

Statements are mailed in December and all taxes are due by December 31, but the bill is not late until later in the year. The Treasurer cites Nebraska Revised Statute 77-204 for the late dates: the first half becomes late on April 1 and the second half on August 1.

Interest on overdue balances is 14% a year under section 77-207, and it accrues daily. The Treasurer offers an online delinquency estimator, which needs the total tax from the property search. If you do not have a statement by December 20, email Customer Service with the parcel number or address.

Nebraska taxes are paid in arrears. In the Board of Equalization's words, the taxes you pay in calendar year 2026 are your 2025 taxes, based on your 2025 valuation. Your 2026 valuation affects the bill you pay in 2027. For a seller, this means the buyer inherits the next valuation, not the one on today's statement.

Overpayments can be refunded. A refund request has to be filed within three years of the tax due date under section 77-1734.01, and the office refunds overpayments to the payer, such as a title or mortgage company.

How do I protest a Douglas County valuation?

File a formal protest with the Board of Equalization between June 1 and June 30. The Assessor's FAQ also describes an informal hearing window of January 15 to February 1 for owners who think the value is above market.

The BOE protest page describes the 2026 rules:

  • Online filing is open June 1 to 11:59 p.m. on June 30.
  • Mailed protests must be postmarked by June 30.
  • Hand-delivered protests were accepted until 6 p.m. on June 30, when the office stayed open late.
  • An appointment with a referee is optional, runs about 15 minutes, and can be in person or by phone.
  • USB drives and discs are not accepted, and photos become public record.

Nebraska law lets anyone file a protest on any property. If the signer is not the owner and has no authorization, the owner is notified by mail. Homes must be valued at actual market value by state law, which the Assessor describes as the likely price the property would sell for.

What is the Douglas County tax sale?

It is a public auction of tax lien certificates for real estate with delinquent taxes. The Treasurer's tax sale page says investors buy a certificate, which is a lien for unpaid taxes, interest and costs. They do not buy the property itself.

  • The Public Tax Sale is online and held on the first Monday in March.
  • Advertising starts the first Thursday in February and runs three weeks.
  • To stay out of the ad, delinquent taxes must be paid by the last Wednesday in January.
  • A Private Tax Sale follows in May, and a Subsequent Tax Sale in mid-September.
  • Owners can redeem within 3 years from the date of sale by paying taxes, interest and fees.

Because the January payment deadline falls before the ads run, an owner behind on taxes has only a short window to clear the balance or arrange a sale.

What happens at the Register of Deeds when a Douglas County house sells?

The deed is recorded in the Assessor/Register of Deeds office, and the Nebraska documentary stamp tax applies. The Department of Revenue now lists $3.32 for each $1,000 of value on deeds recorded from July 18, 2026; its older Chapter 52 regulation text still shows $2.25. Liability rests on the grantor, which is the seller, though the buyer or any agent presenting the deed may pay it.

The register of deeds stamps each deed that is recorded. The sale information from these recordings is what the Assessor then uses to study the market. Exemptions exist, and the Department of Revenue publishes a list, so check it if the transfer is a gift or an estate deed.

Cash Home Buyers can review a Douglas County house with back tax, an open protest or an old lien, and the title company handles payoffs and recording at closing.

Statements are mailed in December and all taxes are due by December 31. The first half becomes late on April 1 and the second half on August 1.

What is the Douglas County property tax protest deadline?

June 30. The formal protest period runs June 1 to June 30, and mailed protests need a June 30 postmark.

What interest does Douglas County charge on late property tax?

The Treasurer states 14% a year under Nebraska statute 77-207, and interest accrues daily.

How long can I redeem after a Douglas County tax sale?

Owners can redeem within 3 years from the date of sale by paying delinquent taxes, interest and fees.

Who pays the documentary stamp tax when I sell in Douglas County?

The grantor, meaning the seller, is liable. Use the current state rate shown above, and the buyer or an agent presenting the deed may pay it.

Where is Red Willow County and what is in it?

Red Willow County lies along Nebraska's southern line, with its south boundary touching Kansas. It covers 718 square miles, nearly all of it land, and the Republican River runs east through the north-central part. The terrain is rolling hills that slope to the east, and the low ground in the river drainage is farmed.

The county was formed in 1873 and named for Red Willow Creek. According to its reference entry, the name is thought to be a mistranslation of the Dakota name Chanshasha Wakpala, which means Red Dogwood Creek. McCook is the county seat. The other incorporated places are the city of Indianola and the villages of Bartley, Danbury and Lebanon, and Marion, Perry and Shippee are unincorporated communities.

Part of the Red Willow Reservoir State Wildlife Management Area is inside the county, and the neighbors are Furnas, Hitchcock and Frontier counties in Nebraska plus Decatur and Rawlins counties in Kansas.

Red Willow County had 10,702 residents in the 2020 census and an estimated 10,307 in 2025, a drop of 3.7 percent. The count has slipped at each census since 1980, when it was 12,615. What is McCook like as a county seat?

McCook was platted in 1882 when the Burlington and Missouri River Railroad reached the site, and it was named for Union Army Brigadier General Alexander McDowell McCook. The city covers about 5.4 square miles.

It is also the home of the first two-year junior college in Nebraska, founded in September 1926 on the second floor of the YMCA building and now part of the Mid-Plains system. The McCook Economic Development Corporation works to keep and attract businesses in the area, and the George Norris House is on the National Register of Historic Places.

How do the weather and the Republican River affect a Red Willow County house?

McCook has a hot-summer humid continental climate with cold, dry winters and hot, humid summers. The annual precipitation normal is 22.53 inches, mostly from May through August, and snowfall averages 28.8 inches a season, mostly from November through April.

  • An average of 45 days a year reach 90 degrees Fahrenheit or higher, and 5.4 days reach 100.
  • About 28 days a year stay at or below freezing all day, and 8.6 days dip to 0 or lower.
  • Records run from minus 30 degrees on January 12, 1912 to 115 on June 26, 2012.

Swings that wide are hard on roofing, siding, exposed plumbing and older windows. Knowing your own list of deferred repairs before you decide how to sell avoids surprises later.

What roads, rail and schools connect Red Willow County?

McCook sits on U.S. Routes 6, 34 and 83, and Nebraska Highway 89 also crosses the county. U.S. 83 runs north to North Platte and Interstate 80, and U.S. 34 links west to Colorado and east toward Hastings and Lincoln.

Amtrak's California Zephyr stops at McCook station. Denver Air Connection runs commercial flights from McCook Regional Airport to Denver.

Who bills Red Willow County property tax, and how is it paid?

The Red Willow County Treasurer collects real estate tax from an office at 502 Norris Avenue in McCook. The mailing address is PO Box 490, McCook, NE 69001, and the phone is 308-345-6515, extension 1. The assessor sets values on all real and personal property, keeps the parcel maps and prepares the tax roll for the treasurer. The office also answers questions about homestead exemption eligibility.

What can change a Red Willow County valuation?

The assessor's page names four things that move a value: shifts in the market, outside influences on the property, adding or removing improvements, and a remodel or rehab. A new garage or a finished basement raises the number, and tearing down an old outbuilding should lower it.

If you disagree, the protest must reach the County Clerk on or before June 30 and must give the value you are asking for and the reasons. Under Statute 77-1502, the clerk mails the board's decision by August 2, and you then have until August 24 to appeal to the Tax Equalization and Review Commission under Statute 77-1510. Exemptions are available for educational and religious facilities and for qualifying seniors or people with disabilities.

What happens at the Red Willow County tax sale?

The county holds its tax sale on the first Monday in March, and the 2026 sale was March 2 in the courthouse. The delinquent list is advertised for three consecutive weeks in February in the local paper and online.

  • A buyer purchases the delinquent tax, not the property, and pays later years' taxes as they come due.
  • The redemption period is three years at 14 percent interest.
  • If the owner has not redeemed after three years, the certificate holder has six months to foreclose.
  • Registration costs $25 and the county charges $20 per certificate sold.

The treasurer's page says the office will not give legal advice to certificate buyers and points them to Nebraska statutes 77-1801 through 77-1941, so an attorney is the right call for your own parcel.

How does a Red Willow County sale close with tax owed?

The title company asks the treasurer for the payoff, collects it from the proceeds and records the deed. The seller also pays Nebraska's documentary stamp tax through the register of deeds, which the Department of Revenue sets at $3.32 for each $1,000 of value for deeds recorded from July 18, 2026.

If the taxes have already gone to the March sale, redeeming the certificate has to come first. Send us the parcel number and we can look at the numbers with you.

When do Red Willow County taxes become delinquent?

The first half becomes delinquent May 1 and the second half September 1. The dates follow Nebraska Statute 77-204, so unpaid first-half tax is delinquent from May 1.

How do I protest my Red Willow County valuation?

Send your protest to the County Clerk on or before June 30, stating the value you are asking for and why. The county board of equalization hears it, and its decision can be appealed to the state commission.

It is the annual sale of tax certificates for unpaid real estate tax, held the first Monday in March. Certificates carry 14 percent interest, and the county's page gives a three-year redemption period.

The 2020 census counted 5,157 housing units, with 12.1 percent vacant. Population fell to 10,702 in 2020 and to an estimated 10,307 in 2025.

Sarpy County by the numbers

Where is Sarpy County and why is it different from the rest of Nebraska?

Sarpy County is the smallest county in Nebraska by area and the third most populous. It covers 247.5 square miles, with the Missouri River on its east side and the Platte River along the south and west, and it is part of the Omaha-Council Bluffs metropolitan area. Douglas County lies to the north.

The land is low rolling hills cut by small gullies that carry groundwater to one of the two rivers. The county was carved out of Douglas County by the Territorial Legislature on February 7, 1857, and takes its name from Peter Sarpy, an early fur trader at Fontenelle's Post in the Bellevue area. Papillion is the county seat and Bellevue is the largest city. The other cities are Gretna, La Vista and Springfield.

What is the Offutt Air Force Base connection?

Offutt Air Force Base, just south of Bellevue, is a major part of the county's history and identity. The Army post there, Fort Crook, was set up in the 1890s and added Offutt Field in the 1920s. During World War II the Glenn L. Martin plant built more than 2,000 aircraft, including the B-29s Enola Gay and Bockscar. Offutt was Strategic Air Command headquarters in the Cold War and is the home of U.S. Strategic Command today.

Military families move on orders, and a house can need to sell on a fixed timeline. A permanent change of station does not wait for a listing to find a buyer, so a seller in that position should compare how long each way of selling is likely to take.

The county grew by about 17,700 people between 2020 and the 2025 estimate. Houses with deferred repairs, liens or tax problems are the ones owners often struggle to sell the usual way.

What communities and school districts does Sarpy County include?

Beyond the five cities, the census recognizes places such as Chalco, La Platte, Linoma Beach, Melia, Richfield and Beacon View, plus the Offutt AFB census-designated place. Avery, Gilmore, Meadow and Portal are unincorporated.

  • Springfield Platteview Community Schools, Louisville Public Schools and Ashland-Greenwood Public Schools

Because so many districts overlap, two houses a block apart can be billed by different school districts and carry different totals. Read the tax district code on your statement before comparing.

How do roads and transit work in Sarpy County?

Interstate 80 crosses the county, along with U.S. Highways 6 and 75 and Nebraska Highways 31, 50, 85 and 370. Metro Transit from Omaha serves the county, and in Papillion that means Route 93 on weekdays.

Because the county adjoins Omaha, the commute and the school district are two things a buyer will weigh, along with the condition of the house.

Why are Sarpy County tax dates different?

Sarpy has more than 100,000 people, so it follows the larger-county schedule in Nebraska Statute 77-204: the first half is delinquent April 1 and the second half August 1, not May 1 and September 1. For the 2025 tax statement, the county lists April 1, 2026 and August 1, 2026 as the dates of delinquency, and its first installment was due March 31, 2026 at the Treasurer's Office, 1102 E. 1st Street in Papillion.

An April 1 delinquency can catch a seller who plans around the May 1 date used in most of the state. If you are selling in the spring, ask the treasurer what is already due.

How does a Sarpy County valuation protest work?

The county assessor certifies new values on or before June 1 and mails a Notice of Valuation Change only to owners whose value changed. A value represents market value as of January 1, and the assessor uses mass appraisal with cost, income and sales comparison approaches. Agricultural land is assessed at 75 percent of market value under the Nebraska Constitution.

If you disagree, Protest Form 422 can be filed only from June 1 to June 30. The form is accepted at the County Clerk's office, online or by mail, up to 4:45 p.m. on June 30. If the 30th falls on a weekend, the deadline moves to the next business day. Forms postmarked or received before June 1 are returned to sender. Include your reasons, a description of the property, a signature, a date and the parcel number, and cross out personal data, since protests are public records.

The board can hire independent appraisers as referees to help review protests. Statute 77-1502 gives owners in counties over 100,000 the right to meet in person with the board or a referee, and lets those counties extend the hearing window from July 25 to August 10. The county's guidance says to present evidence that the assessor valued the property above market or out of line with similar properties.

A board decision can be appealed to the Tax Equalization and Review Commission at 301 Centennial Mall S. in Lincoln, phone 402-471-2842, on or before August 24, or September 10 when the county extended its hearings.

What happens to a delinquent Sarpy County parcel?

The Treasurer publishes the delinquent tax list in the Omaha Daily Record, and the county posts a Tax Sale Information page. Buyers at a tax sale purchase the delinquent amount, and Nebraska law (statutes 77-1801 to 77-1941) governs what happens if the owner does not redeem. Because the county's tax sale page did not load fully when we checked, we are not stating its exact dates or fees here.

The safe course is to phone the treasurer for a payoff figure before a closing date is set.

What should a Sarpy County seller expect at closing?

The title company collects the tax payoff from the sale proceeds, and the seller pays the documentary stamp tax through the register of deeds. The Department of Revenue lists $3.32 per $1,000 of value for deeds recorded on or after July 18, 2026, and Form 521 is filed with the deed.

If a house in Bellevue, Papillion, La Vista, Gretna or Springfield needs work you do not want to pay for, send us the address and we will explain what an as-is sale would look like.

Only from June 1 to June 30. Forms received before June 1 or postmarked after June 30 are not accepted, and the deadline is 4:45 p.m. on June 30 at the County Clerk's office.

Where is Madison County, Nebraska, and which towns does it include?

Madison County is in northeast Nebraska, with the city of Madison as county seat and Norfolk as the center of local employment. It covers about 575 square miles, of which roughly 573 are land, and the Elkhorn River crosses the upper central part of the county on its way east.

Besides Madison and Norfolk, the county includes the cities of Battle Creek, Newman Grove (partly) and Tilden (partly), plus the village of Meadow Grove. Emerick, Enola, Kalamazoo and Warnerville are unincorporated communities. The neighbors are Wayne, Stanton, Platte, Boone, Antelope and Pierce counties.

The terrain is gently rolling, sloping to the east-southeast, and largely used for agriculture. The county's assessor offers online maps showing assessor parcels, flood plain and zoning, which are worth opening before you list a rural or river-adjacent property.

How did Madison County come about?

Madison County was created on January 26, 1856 and organized on January 21, 1868. It was likely named for Madison, Wisconsin, where many early residents came from, and that city in turn was named for President James Madison.

Growth followed in the next decades. Census counts rose from 1,133 in 1870 to 16,976 in 1900 and 26,037 in 1930, and the county reached 35,585 residents in 2020. For sellers, the county has an employment-heavy Norfolk and a set of smaller towns, Madison, Battle Creek, Newman Grove and Tilden, where lots and acreage are the norm. When are Madison County property taxes due?

  • Payment search is available on Nebraska Taxes Online for Madison County.

If taxes are not paid, the personal property lien means any personal property you own, taxable or not, can be seized to satisfy the debt. A seller with a business on the property should ask the treasurer about both real and personal accounts.

Who sets Madison County's tax levies, and where can you read them?

Many separate bodies set the levy on a Madison County bill, and the assessor publishes a certification of values for each. The 2026 certifications, posted in August 2026, cover cities, the county, the Ag Society, the Airport Authority, Natural Resources Districts, Educational Service Units, fire districts, Northeast Community College, the Norfolk Parking District, railroad transportation safety, sanitary districts, school bonds and school districts.

The assessor also posts tax increment financing project sheets for Madison, Newman Grove, Norfolk and Tilden. If your parcel is inside one of these projects, part of the tax may be directed to the redevelopment project, so ask the assessor how that affects your parcel.

The assessor's page also links to Nebraska's homestead exemption information, exemption rules for religious, charitable and educational property, and the Form 422 protest instructions.

What does the Madison County assessor do?

The Madison County Assessor's mission is to achieve equalization among all classes of property by keeping high standards in mass appraisal and accurate property and land records. The office also says it aims to manage county growth with technological tools that speed up the flow of information to the public.

Three practical uses of the assessor's website help a seller:

  • The online valuation records let you see how the property is classified and valued before you talk to a buyer.
  • The definitions page explains what counts as real property, personal property, agricultural land and greenbelt land.
  • The homestead information link leads to the state rules for the exemption, and a separate link covers the exemption for religious, charitable and educational property.

For a house with a detached shop or equipment on site, check whether any of it is personal property, because that is assessed and billed separately from the land and buildings.

How does a Madison County protest or sale work?

Protests of valuation in Madison County are filed on Nebraska Form 422, and the county's Board of Equalization conducts the hearings, and county minutes from 2024 and 2025 show hearings held on June 25. State rules put real property protests due by June 30, and an appeal of the board's ruling goes to the Tax Equalization and Review Commission within 30 days after adjournment.

When you sell, Nebraska's documentary stamp tax is $3.32 for each $1,000 of value for deeds recorded on or after July 18, 2026. The seller pays it as grantor. The deed must come with Form 521, the Real Estate Transfer Statement, or the register of deeds will not accept it for recording.

More questions about Madison County, NE Property Tax Guide

When are Madison County, Nebraska property taxes due?

They are due December 31. The first half is delinquent the following May 1 and the second half on September 1.

Who do I call at the Madison County treasurer's office?

Call 402-454-3311, extension 133, for the treasurer, Donna Primrose. The assessor's extension is 160, and both offices are in the courthouse at 1313 North Main Street in Madison.

What are the biggest employers in Madison County?

Norfolk Nebraska Economic Development lists Tyson Fresh Meats in Madison with 1,470 employees and Faith Regional Health Services in Norfolk with 1,384. Northeast Community College, Norfolk Public Schools and the Nucor divisions follow.

How do I protest my Madison County valuation?

File Nebraska Form 422 with the county clerk by June 30 for real property. The Board of Equalization holds hearings, and further appeals go to the Tax Equalization and Review Commission within 30 days.

Do unpaid Madison County taxes create a lien on personal property?

Yes. Personal property taxes become a first lien on all personal property you own on the due date, and unpaid taxes can lead to seizure of that property.

Where is Platte County and how is it laid out?

Platte County sits in east-central Nebraska, with Columbus as the county seat. The Census Bureau lists 684.59 square miles, of which 675.12 is land, which makes it the 42nd-largest Nebraska county by area.

The Platte River runs east along the county's south line, and the Loup River crosses the lower part of the county and joins the Platte near Columbus. The ground is low rolling hills, mostly farmland, that slope toward the east-southeast. Platte County was created on January 26, 1856, and borders Colfax, Butler, Polk, Merrick, Nance, Boone, Madison and Stanton counties.

Besides Columbus, the incorporated places are the cities of Humphrey and part of Newman Grove, and the villages of Cornlea, Creston, Duncan, Lindsay, Monroe, Platte Center and Tarnov. Lakeview is a census-designated place. A house in any of them is billed by the same county treasurer, but the school and city levies on the bill differ from one town to the next.

What does Platte County look like in numbers?

Platte County had 34,296 residents in the 2020 census and an estimated 35,649 in 2025. The table pulls together the figures that matter most when a seller is thinking about who the likely buyers are.

ItemFigure
Population, 2020 census34,296

Median household income, 2024 ACS estimate$71,552
Median age, 2020 census38.3 years
Residents age 65 or older, 202017.5%

Population has grown in every census since 1990, from 29,820 then to 34,296 in 2020.

What drives the economy around Columbus?

Columbus is an agriculture and manufacturing town, and its industry grew up around cheap, plentiful hydroelectric power. Large employers named in the city's reference entry include Becton Dickinson, which runs two plants, Behlen Manufacturing, Cargill's ground-beef plant, an Archer Daniels Midland corn-milling facility, Vishay Dale Electronics and FLEXcon.

On the public side, Nebraska Public Power District is headquartered in Columbus, and Columbus Community Hospital and Columbus Public Schools are also major employers. Central Community College has a campus about four miles northwest of the city; it opened in 1969 as Platte Junior College and was the first county-supported college in the state.

With that many large employers, a job change or transfer can put a house on the market on short notice. A seller in that spot often cares more about a firm closing date than about a long listing period.

How does Platte County's weather and river setting affect a house?

Columbus has a hot-summer humid continental climate, with cold, dry winters and hot, humid summers. Precipitation averages 26.87 inches a year and falls mostly between April and October, with the peak in late spring and early summer. The record high is 115 degrees Fahrenheit.

Two things follow for an older house. Summer storms test roofs, gutters and basement drainage, and a house close to the Loup or Platte deserves a flood check before listing. The 2019 Midwest flooding reached Columbus, where a man died after a bridge collapsed while he tried to help someone stranded in the water. Keep repair records, insurance claims and any elevation paperwork together so you can answer a buyer's questions about water.

What roads, schools and services serve Platte County?

U.S. Highways 30 and 81 are the main routes, along with Nebraska Highways 22, 39, 45 and 91. Express Arrow is the transit service listed for the county.

  • Columbus Public Schools (District 1) and Lakeview Community Schools (District 5)
  • Humphrey Public Schools (District 67) and Newman Grove Public Schools (District 13)
  • Twin River Public Schools in Genoa, Leigh Community Schools, Clarkson Public Schools and St. Edward Public Schools
  • Madison Public Schools, which also reaches into the county

Which district a house falls in sets the school levy on the tax bill, so check the district code on the statement before you compare your taxes with a neighbor's.

Who bills and collects property tax in Platte County?

The Platte County Treasurer bills and collects all real estate and personal property taxes. The office is on the first floor, west side, of the courthouse at 2610 14th Street in Columbus, and the number is 402-563-4913. Hours are Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., with the second Thursday of each month starting at 8:30.

You can pay through Nebraska Taxes Online, by mail, or in the drop box by the west entrance. The treasurer's page says a card payment carries a 2.49 percent charge and a debit card $2.95. Notices go out between late November and December, and anyone who does not get one should call the office.

StepDate or rule
Taxes dueDecember 31
First half delinquentThe following May 1
Second half delinquentThe following September 1
Interest on delinquent tax14 percent statutory rate
Valuation protest filingOn or before June 30, with the County Clerk
Appeal of a board decisionTax Equalization and Review Commission, by August 24

Platte County also posts a Delinquent Tax Listing on the treasurer's page, and it links the county's tax levy booklet, which shows the levy for each taxing district.

How do you protest a Platte County valuation?

File Form 422 with the County Clerk by June 30, one form for each parcel. The Platte County Assessor's page points owners to the state form, and the clerk's page says the completed form goes to the County Board of Equalization through the clerk's office. A hearing date is then set before the board.

Under Nebraska Statute 77-1502, the protest must state the reason, the value you want and enough documentation for the board to reach a different number. A protest without those items is dismissed, and so is one filed after June 30. The clerk mails the decision by August 2, and under Statute 77-1510 an owner who disagrees can appeal to the state commission on or before August 24.

The same form can be used when the assessor adds omitted property or imposes a penalty. A recent appraisal, a repair estimate for deferred work, or sales of similar nearby houses are the usual evidence.

What happens when Platte County taxes go unpaid?

Unpaid real estate tax can end up in the county's tax sale each March, where investors buy the delinquent amount as a certificate, not the house itself. The county's March 2026 report showed 244 properties on the list, 138 parcels offered on sale day, 119 certificates sold, and 24 registered buyers with 22 who showed up.

Platte's tax sale rules sheet was not reachable when we checked, but other Nebraska counties publish a three-year redemption period and a six-month foreclosure window after that. For an owner, that means a delinquent bill is a countdown, not just a penalty. Paying the balance, or selling before the clock runs out, ends the exposure.

What is different about selling a Platte County house with tax due?

Start by asking the treasurer for the balance on the parcel, since a title company will want back taxes cleared at closing. Then plan for the state's deed tax: the documentary stamp tax is paid by the seller and collected by the register of deeds. The Department of Revenue lists the rate as $3.32 for each $1,000 of value for deeds recorded on or after July 18, 2026, and the deed packet includes Form 521, the Real Estate Transfer Statement.

Inherited houses, rentals with a tenant and houses with unfinished repairs are the usual cases we see. If you want a straight answer on what a sale would involve, send us the address and we will tell you what we can and cannot do.

More questions about Platte County, NE Property Tax Guide

When are Platte County property taxes due?

Taxes are due December 31. The first half becomes delinquent the following May 1 and the second half the following September 1, and the county applies a 14 percent statutory rate to delinquencies.

Where do I file a Platte County valuation protest?

File Form 422 with the County Clerk in Columbus on or before June 30. Each parcel needs its own protest, with your reason, requested value and supporting documents.

Can I pay Platte County taxes online?

Yes. The treasurer directs payers to Nebraska Taxes Online, and mail and the courthouse drop box by the west entrance also work. Cards add a 2.49 percent charge, and debit cards $2.95.

What is the Platte County Treasurer's phone number?

The treasurer's office can be reached at 402-563-4913. It is at 2610 14th Street in Columbus, open weekdays 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

Does Platte County hold a tax sale?

Yes. The treasurer's page reports a public tax sale in March 2026 with 244 properties on the list and 119 certificates sold. Tax sale rules and the delinquent listing are posted on the treasurer's page.

Who pays the deed tax when a Platte County house sells?

The seller does. Nebraska's documentary stamp tax falls on the grantor and is collected by the register of deeds, at $3.32 per $1,000 of value for deeds recorded on or after July 18, 2026.
